name: High-Plank Crossbody Drag
definition: An alternating high-plank anti-rotation drill in which one dumbbell or kettlebell rests near one hand or beneath the torso, the opposite hand drags the single implement across the floor, and the athlete re-establishes two-hand support before repeating from the other side. The NSCA bridge pull-through owns the dumbbell fixture; the Prehab guide owns the kettlebell fixture. The training-defining task is resisting spinal extension and rotation while support changes; the arm drag is not assigned an unsupported prime joint action, and the authored stabilizer roles are bounded anatomy-and-mechanics inferences rather than exact-fixture recruitment measurements. Implement mass is logged once but is non-comparable because floor friction, implement shape, drag distance, and body geometry materially change demand. Renegade rows, multiple-implement transfers, forearm planks, push-ups, carries, and same-side pulls remain outside this family.

variantAxes.description: The repetition starts in a two-palm high plank.
One palm and both feet support the body during the drag.
The opposite hand drags the implement beneath the torso to the other side.
The shoulders and hips stay square.
Log the single implement mass once.
The implement slides freely across the floor.

exerciseRules.description: Dumbbell equipment uses the dumbbell shape.
Kettlebell equipment uses the kettlebell shape.

execution.startingPosition: Set a high plank with palms down, elbows straight, and one dumbbell just behind one hand. Log the single dumbbell mass once.
execution.movement: Shift support toward the hand beside the dumbbell, lift the opposite hand, and pull the dumbbell across toward the lifting arm's shoulder.
execution.endpoint: Set the dumbbell down with the hips and shoulders still parallel to the floor.
execution.returnPhase: Replace the dragging hand to re-establish high plank before repeating with the other arm.
execution.controlledJoints: Resist low-back sag and trunk rotation throughout the pull-through.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the supporting palm and both feet firmly planted.
execution.sideOrDirection: Alternate sides; count each completed pull-through as one repetition and use an even total.
disqualifyingCompensations: Rowing the dumbbell off the floor changes the exercise.
Using two dumbbells changes the single-implement topology.
Turning the hips toward the load loses the anti-rotation task.

execution.startingPosition: Set a high plank with one kettlebell beneath the chest. Log the single kettlebell mass once.
execution.movement: Shift support to one side, use the opposite hand to grasp the kettlebell, and slide it across toward that arm.
execution.endpoint: Finish at the farthest comfortable point that preserves the high-plank position.
execution.returnPhase: Replace the dragging hand, then use the other hand to drag the kettlebell back in the opposite direction.
execution.controlledJoints: Resist low-back sag and trunk rotation throughout the pull-through.
execution.supportAndPosture: Keep the supporting palm and both feet firmly planted.
execution.sideOrDirection: Alternate sides; count each completed pull-through as one repetition and use an even total.
disqualifyingCompensations: Rowing the kettlebell off the floor changes the exercise.
Using two kettlebells changes the single-implement topology.
Turning the hips toward the load loses the anti-rotation task.
